# Scotiabank (BNS) and Value Stocks Deep Dive Analysis

Report 057 | Published 2021-05-23 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-5-23/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/057.json)

Liquidity, inflation and banks.

Several calendar forecasts are sharply testable: May CPI above 4.5% and infrastructure enactment were right, while a summer inflation peak and no substantial 2022 rate hikes were wrong. The GBTC discussion identifies the discount mechanism but mistakenly calls a lockup-dependent premium trade risk-free. Bank risks require more care: rising rates can produce acute losses, not merely slow margin erosion.

**Coverage:** All sections read, including portfolio rotations, closed-end trust mechanics, four bank-risk categories and conditional macro scenarios. Short current COVID counts and individual balance-sheet statistics are incidental; all material investment and causal conclusions are retained. The article contains explicit inflation and rate deadlines that are scored separately.

| Author modality | asserted |

Banks create deposits when lending; they do not lend central-bank reserves to households or mechanically multiply a supplied reserve stock. QE can buy from nonbanks and directly create deposits.

**Direction:** Contradicted for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Money creation in the modern economy](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/-/media/boe/files/quarterly-bulletin/2014/money-creation-in-the-modern-economy.pdf) | Bank of England | Verified in the audit

2014 Q1 bulletin: bank lending creates deposits; reserves are not multiplied into loans. QE can buy from nonbanks, directly increasing their deposits as well as bank reserves.
